ROLL CALL: At 6:05 p.m., on Monday, January 27, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, WANG
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Deputy Director of Public Works and Utilities
Ramos, Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services
LohGuan, Director of Human Resources Ko, Manager Analyst Alvarez, Deputy Director of Parks and
Recreation Houghton, Assistant Chief of Police Fuentes

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Wang

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  COMMENDATIONS: WINNERS OF THE 2024 HOLIDAY HOME DECORATING
  CONTEST – F2M25-3

  Mayor Wang and the Alhambra City Council, on behalf of the citizens of Alhambra, wished to
  recognize and congratulate the winning contestants from the City’s 2024 Holiday Home

  presentation, which is on file in the City Clerk’s office. This contest invited residents to show
  their sense of community and holiday spirit through the use of holiday decorations on their
  homes. The winners were commended for displaying extraordinary efforts in enhancing and
  promoting a family-oriented community through their colorful and imaginative holiday displays.
  Mayor WANG presented commendations to the winners of the 2024 Holiday Home Decorating

  Mayor Wang and the City Council wished to commend and thank Deputy Director of Utilities

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS (TIME LIMITATIONS: 5 MINUTES PER

  1) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., discussed the Historic Preservation Commission and the process

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., distributed handouts to Council which are on file in

PUBLIC HEARING

3.  PUBLIC HEARING TO CONSIDER A RESOLUTION CERTIFYING AN EIR, INCLUDING
THE RESPONSE TO COMMENTS; ADOPTING FINDINGS OF FACT AND A  STATEMENT
OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS; APPROVING THE MMRP; APPROVING  THE
COMMUNITY CENTER PROJECT ON THE SITE OF THE FORMER  HEALTH CLINIC ON
SHORB STREET BETWEEN 6TH AND 7TH STREETS, LOCATED AT 612 WEST SHORB
STREET ON A SITE OF 1.77 ACRES; AND APPROVING A PARCEL MAP FOR THE PROJECT,
INCLUDING A VACATION OF A PORTION OF  SHORB STREET, LOCATED BETWEEN 6TH
AND 7TH STREETS AND DIRECTING  ISSUANCE OF A NOTICE INVITING BIDS – F2M22-
65, N2M25-8, R2M25-4

  2
1-27-25
   This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M25-8 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to consider approval of the Alhambra Community Center Project at a 1.77-acre site
  located at 612 West Shorb Street, between 6th and 7th streets. Director of Parks and
  Recreation MACIAS delivered a staff report. Approval of the Project would include approval of
  a parcel map, aggregating lots and vacating Shorb Street between 6th and 7th to facilitate the
  Project. The Council would consider certification of an EIR for the project, including the
  associated response to comments, mitigation monitoring and reporting program, findings and
  statement of overriding considerations.

  The City of Alhambra is the owner of the Property located at 612 West Shorb Street, located
  between 6th and 7th streets. The Property was the site of a historic building that was formerly
  a health clinic, but which was vacant for decades. In 2020 the City Council began imagining a
  use for the Property, and determined that construction of a community center on the site would
  provide a much-needed amenity for the local neighborhood, as well as the City of Alhambra at
  large. Unfortunately, the City did not have funding for such a project at that time. In April 2023,
  the City received a grant from the State for construction of a community center in the amount
  of 25 million dollars, thanks to the efforts of California Senator Susan Rubio and State
  Assemblymember Mike Fong. The City then retained an architect, project manager and
  environmental consultant to prepare designs for consideration by the City Council and
  Alhambra community. The Council held public meetings to consider design options on October
  25, 2023 (on site), March 11, 2024 and June 18, 2024. Approval of the project requires an
  environmental evaluation under the California Environmental Quality Act. Options were
  included in the project studied in the event that additional funding became available during the
  processing of the project, ranging from 17,000 square feet, up to 25,000 square feet. Currently,
  the City projected the current available funding would be sufficient to construct the 17,000
  square foot project, but the project would be designed to enable additions if funding becomes
  available in future years.

  The City determined that it would prepare a full Environmental Impact Report (EIR) for the
  project. Pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15082, the City circulated a Notice of
  Preparation (NOP) together with the Initial Study to State, regional, and local agencies,
  interested organizations, and members of the public for a 30-day period, commencing May
  28, 2024, and ending June 27, 2024. Based on public input and the results of the Initial Study,
  the Draft EIR addressed environmental effects in the following areas: Biological Resources
  (special-status species and the movement of wildlife species), Cultural Resources (historic
  and archaeological resources), Geology and Soils (paleontological resources), Noise (all
  except airport land use plan, private airstrip), and Tribal Cultural Resources. The Draft EIR
  determined that impacts to biological resources, archaeological resources, paleontological
  resources, noise and vibration, and tribal cultural resources would be less than significant with
  the incorporation of mitigation measures. Additionally, the current Property to be utilized for
  the Project was comprised of multiple parcels. The California Building Code prohibits
  construction of buildings across lot lines. Further, the Project also contemplated construction
  within the existing Shorb Street right-of-way, between 6th and 7th streets. The Subdivision Map
  Act allows these parcels to be joined into one lot to allow for construction of the project if the
  Council approves a parcel map for the site. Finally, the next step in the progress of the Project
  would be to direct staff and the City’s consultants to prepare a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  17,000 square foot Project. The proposed resolution directed staff to do so, and return to
  Council with a proposed award of contract for construction.

  The Project was described at length in the Final EIR document (comprised of the Draft EIR,
  written comments, responses to comments, and minor revisions/clarifications to the Draft EIR
  and the MMRP), are available through the City of Alhambra’s website here:
  https://www.cityofalhambra.org/743/Alhambra-Community-Center-Project.

  Open Public Hearing: Mayor WANG opened the public hearing.
  3
1-27-25
   Public Comment:  Suzi DUNKEL-SOTO, 2213 Winthrop Dr., noted a typo in the staff
  report and agenda which omitted the role Senator Susan Rubio played in securing the funding
  for the community center in the State budget. She requested that this be noted and that if
  there were any naming of the community center, that Council consider State Senator Rubio.
  City Attorney MONTES noted the correction.

  Close Public Hearing: After receiving public comment, Mayor WANG closed the public
  hearing.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked her fellow subcommittee
  member Mr. Maza and discussed the opportunities offered by the community center.
  Councilmember MALONEY expressed excitement and thanked Ms. Andrade-Stadler, Mr.
  Maza and staff for their work on the project. He also thanked the community members, the
  Historic Preservation Group and the Historical Society for their input on the project. He briefly
  discussed the continued process in completing the project. Councilmember MAZA thanked
  Ms. Andrade-Stadler for her work on the sub-committee, the Historic Preservation Group, the
  Historical Society, and City staff for their work. He also discussed the benefits and
  opportunities presented by the community center and the process to complete the project.
  Vice Mayor LEE thanked State Senator Susan Rubio and Assemblymember Fong for their
  contributions in securing funding and discussed the opportunities of the project. She discussed
  the need for historic preservation. Mayor WANG echoed her fellow Councilmembers,
  comments.

  Action Taken:  City Council conducted a public hearing and thereafter adopted
  Resolution No. R2M25-4 entitled: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF ALHAMBRA CERTIFYING AN EIR, INCLUDING THE RESPONSE TO COMMENTS;
  ADOPTING FINDINGS OF FACT AND A STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING
  CONSIDERATIONS; APPROVING THE MMRP; APPROVING THE COMMUNITY CENTER
  PROJECT ON THE SITE OF THE FORMER HEALTH CLINIC ON SHORB STREET
  BETWEEN 6TH AND 7TH STREETS, LOCATED AT 612 WEST SHORB STREET ON A SITE
  OF 1.77 ACRES; AND APPROVING A PARCEL MAP FOR THE PROJECT, INCLUDING A
  VACATION OF A PORTION OF SHORB STREET, LOCATED BETWEEN 6TH AND 7TH
  STREETS AND DIRECTING ISSUANCE OF A NOTICE INVITING BIDS

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

4.  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 AND RESOLUTION
  ADOPTING FY 2024-25 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS – F2M23-17, R2M25-2

  Director of Finance LIEU delivered a staff report and presentation, which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted the Budget for Fiscal Years 2023-
  24 and 2024-25, which appropriated funds and approved revenue projections for the fiscal
  year. During the fiscal year, unforeseen financial needs and opportunities typically arise, which
  require City Council approval of recommended adjustments to projected revenues and
  expenditures. Staff presented a mid-year Budget review to provide a Budget update for FY
  2024-25. The Director of Finance provided the City Council with a high-level overview of the
  FY 2023-24 actual performance and updated budget projections for FY 2024-25. Staff also
  requested that the City Council approve a resolution adopting the FY 2024-25 Budget
  adjustments.
  4
1-27-25
   Discussion:  Council thanked Ms. Lieu for her presentation. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. LIEU discussed the Measure AL Sales Tax. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER discussed the San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing Trust Fund membership.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Mid-Year Budget Review and
  related reports; and, adopt Resolution No. R2M25-2 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra
  City Council adopting Fiscal Year 2024-25 Budget adjustments of the City of Alhambra, Golf
  Course Clubhouse Corporation, Alhambra Capital Improvements Corporation, Alhambra
  Parking Authority, Alhambra Facilities Financing Authority and the Alhambra Public Financing
  Authority

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG

  Absent:  NONE

5.  INCENTIVES FOR COMMERCIAL USE ON GROUND FLOOR OF MIXED-USE
  BUILDINGS AND REVIEW DEVELOPMENT FOR EAST MAIN STREET (BUILDING
  HEIGHTS) – F2M24-33

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report and presentation which is on
  file in the City Clerk’s office. As part of the City Council’s 2024 Strategic Plan, the Council
  wanted to identify incentives for commercial uses on the ground floor of mixed-use buildings
  (Goal 3.7) and wanted to review development for E. Main Street with regard to building heights
  (Goal 3.9). Since both goals were inter-related, both items were being brought forward for
  discussion at the same time to further the Council’s Strategic Plan Goal 6.2 to promote
  Citywide mixed-use development with housing. Staff presented to the Council additional
  context as it related to Incentives for Commercial Use on Ground Floor of Mixed-Use Buildings
  as well as tools the Council could consider in incentivizing mixed-use development including:
  Flexible Development Standards, Additional Density and Elimination of the Residential
  Planned Development Permit. Staff also presented a review of development for E. Main Street
  with respect to building heights. Should the City Council direct staff to make changes to
  existing development standards, staff would prepare the appropriate zone text amendments
  and have them reviewed by the Planning Commission for their input prior to returning to the
  Council for final approval.

  Mayor WANG offered clarification regarding public concerns with regards to building height.
  She recounted the Council’s past action, the past action of the Planning Commission, and
  discussed the intention of the current agenda item.

  Public Comment:

  The following speakers expressed concerns regarding changes to the RPD process and
  opposed any changes to the maximum building height limits in the East Main Corridor:

  1) Bert NG, 203 S. Cordova St.
  2) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St.
  3) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St.
  4) Cody CORBETT, 217 S. Granada Ave.
  5) Andrew, 32 N. Almansor
  6) Marie LOPEZ, 2821 Poplar Blvd.
  7) Olga MICHAELS, Lindaraxa Park N.
  8) Brad MICHAELS, Lindaraxa Park
  9) Lawrence MARCHESE
  10) Ari GUTIERREZ ARAMBULA, via Zoom
  5
1-27-25
   11) Ibeth, via Zoom
  12) Bertha RIVERA
  13) Bernice ORTEGA, 227 S. El Molino St.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor LEE expressed disgust over continued discussion of building
  height in the East Main Corridor and stated that she would hold to her promise to maintain a
  maximum building height of 35 feet. She questioned why the item was brought forward to the
  Council.

  Councilmember MAZA offered clarification as to the item and the Strategic Planning goal to
  provide Council with options for incentives for development. He stated that Council did not
  intend to make any changes with regards to maximum building heights. He stressed the need
  to clarify any rumors or confusion among the public. He stated that the item was at the direction
  of Council during the Strategic Planning session. He spoke to the unique qualities of the East
  Main Corridor east of Almansor St. and the sincere intention to maintain its overall character
  despite limited options for commercial development. He clarified that there was no intention to
  change the project proposed for 801 E. Main St. He thanked staff for their presentation of
  options to incentivize commercial development at the direction of Council.

  Councilmember MALONEY further clarified that the presentation did not involve any changes
  to the proposed project at 801 E. Main St. He addressed questions proposed by Ms. Lee and
  clarified the item was a result of the last Strategic Planning process that Ms. Lee was absent
  from which brought about the evening’s presentation. Ms. LEE and Mr. MALONEY discussed
  the presentation. Mr. MALONEY continued to clarify the intention of providing incentives for
  commercial development, the Council approved building height limit of 35 feet, the public
  support for an Old Town Alhambra district, and the need to balance residential and commercial
  development. He went on to discuss the vacant commercial properties on East Main St. and
  the need to create a vibrant commercial corridor. He stated that he did not want to raise the
  height limit in the East Main Corridor. He reiterated his previous suggestion to allow developers
  an extra 3 feet in overall building height if they agreed to construct a mixed-use development,
  however he added that he would accept the wishes of the Council and the community. He
  discussed the upcoming Strategic Planning session. He continued to stress that this was not
  an action item.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke regarding the qualities of Alhambra’s
  commercial corridor and the benefits of mixed-use developments. She assured the public that
  Council understood the public’s views regarding building heights. She praised the renditions
  provided by Mr. Ho for potential mixed-use developments for fitting in with the character of Old
  Town Alhambra. She stated that she supported maintaining the previously agreed upon
  building height limit.

  Mayor WANG and Mr. HO discussed the reference of the 801 E. Main St. as an example of a
  potential developments and that there were no changes proposed to the project. They went
  on to discuss the incentives for mixed use development as they would relate to compliance
  with HCD regulations. Ms. WANG stated that she wanted to respect the previous decision of
  City Council with regards to building heights and assured the public that she did not want to
  revisit that discussion. She stated that she supported the limit of 3 story building heights but
  discussed the ceiling height differences and trends in commercial and residential
  developments. She stated that recent trends raised ceiling heights and raised windows as
  more desirable qualities for attracting businesses. She proposed a compromise wherein
  Council would flex the development standard on a case-by-case basis in order to attract quality
  businesses. She suggested that staff could bring back an update at a later time.

  Mr. MAZA thanked Ms. Wang for her explanation of ceiling heights that would attract larger
  businesses but added that the community was clear in their desire to have smaller businesses
  6
1-27-25
   in an Old Town Alhambra development. He stated that he would be open to her suggestion in
  the area of Main Street from Chapel to Almansor St. Mr. Maza referred to comments made by
  Mr. McCammon regarding a letter shared from Paul Talbot, and clarified that he had no recent
  communications with Mr. Talbot. Mr. Maza continued to address specific comments made by
  the public. Mr. MALONEY disclosed that he did speak with Mr. Talbot regarding interest in
  commercial development.

  Ms. LEE reiterated the need for Council to not entertain actions which would contradict
  previous decisions. She stated that the public relied on the Council to be ethical, responsible,
  and credible. She referred to Mr. Maloney’s comments regarding her absence and stated that
  regardless of her attendance, Council should have considered past decisions. She expressed
  disappointment and outrage at the agenda item and stated that she would discuss the topic at
  the next Strategic Planning session.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 16)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine and were
enacted by one motion.

6.  AMENDMENT TO AXON ENTERPRISES CONTRACT TO INCLUDE DRAFT ONE AND
  ACCEPTANCE OF DONATION FROM ALHAMBRA POLICE FOUNDATION – F2M23-
  6B, C2M23-1, M2M25-8

  On January 9, 2023, the Council awarded a contract to Axon Enterprises, Inc. for the Officer
  Safety Plan 7, which integrates in-car mobile audio video system (MAVS), body-worn camera
  (BWC) system, digital evidence management software, and Taser 7 in an amount not to
  exceed $1,031,582 over five years. On September 25, 2023, City Council approved an
  amendment to add Axon Air in the amount of $51,638.30 through October 2028. On October
  14, 2024, the City Council approved an amendment with Axon Enterprise to include
  Cradlepoint maintenance and virtual reality training aids in a total amount not to exceed
  $1,158,603.13. Staff sought to amend the current contract between the City and Axon
  Enterprises, Inc. to allow for the purchase of three years of Axon Draft One for an increased
  cost of $296,231.20. Axon Draft One was a draft narrative generation tool powered by an
  officer’s BWC. The drafts were generated from the officer’s BWC footage. Sourcewell awarded
  Axon Enterprises, Inc. contract #101223-AXN for Axon Draft One, a contract which would not
  expire until December 15, 2027. Cooperative purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal
  Code 3.36.080(B)(3).

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council amended the contract with Axon Enterprises, Inc. to
  include three (3) years of Axon Draft One in the amount of $296,231.20, for a total amount not
  to exceed $1,427,834.33, subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City
  Attorney; accept a $67,000 donation from the Alhambra Police Foundation (APF) and directed
  the Finance Director to appropriate expenditure and revenue funds to utilize the donation;
  authorized the Chief of Police to execute said agreements; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-8)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  AWARD CONTRACT: PURCHASE OF ONE PICKUP TRUCK FOR THE PARKS
  DEPARTMENT – F2M25-6A, C2M25-6, M2M25-10

  The 2024-25 Budget included the replacement of one pickup truck. The current truck was over
  29 years old and reached its end of service life. As such, staff sought to purchase one pickup
  body truck to replace this vehicle through a cooperative purchase agreement. Cooperative
  purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code 3.36.080(B)(3). On February 8, 2024,
  Sourcewell opened four bids for procuring vehicles, cars, vans, SUVs, and light trucks with
  related equipment, accessories, and services. Sourcewell awarded contract 03824-NAF to
  National Auto Fleet Group on November 4, 2021 - a contract that would not expire until July 9,
  2025. Per the Sourcewell bid specifications, there is the option of purchasing vehicles and
  equipment. Staff recommended purchasing one truck to utilize this option.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to National Auto Fleet Group in the amount of $46,461.95
  for the purchase of one pickup truck; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-10)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  AUTHORIZE RFP: OPERATION OF THE ALHAMBRA CITY JAIL – F2M25-21,
  RFP2M25-1

  The Alhambra City Jail has operated with contract staff for over 20 years. The current contract
  for jail operations would expire June 30, 2025. In the last calendar year, the Alhambra City
  8
1-27-25
   Jaily processed a total of 2,807 arrestees. In addition to processing arrestees, jailers
  transported arrestees to the Alhambra Superior Court. The proposed contract would be for
  five years, with an option for up to three (3) additional one-year extensions at the City’s
  discretion.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) to operate the Alhambra City Jail from qualified companies with proposals due no later
  than 10:00 a.m. on March 12, 2025; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE

10.  RESOLUTION APPROVING A THIRD SIDE LETTER AGREEMENT AMENDING THE
MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING (MOU) BETWEEN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA  AND
THE ALHAMBRA FIREFIGHTERS’ ASSOCIATION – F2M25-2, R2M25-3, C87-16B

  Recently, the Alhambra Firefighters’ Association (AFA) reached out to City staff to request an
  amendment to existing language in the MOU between the City and AFA. In particular, the AFA
  informed the City of the Association’s vote to amend the qualifying date for AFA members
  receiving contributions to the AFA Retiree Medical Trust. The Trust was established and
  managed wholly by the AFA and it legally required certain language pertaining to the Trust be
  included in the MOU between the City and AFA. AFA’s request was to amend the qualifying
  date from February 12, 1993 to July 1, 1994 and to have the new qualifying date reflected in
  the MOU as required by their Trust. There was no financial impact to the City as the Trust was
  owned and managed by AFA.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council took the following actions: 1) Adopted Resolution No.
  R2M25-3 entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra City Council approving a Third Side Letter of
  Agreement amending the Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Alhambra and
  the Alhambra Firefighters’ Association; and, 2) Directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

F2M25-22, F2M25-23, RFP2M25-2, RFP2M25-3

  The City has contracted with St. George’s Medical Clinic for pre-employment medical and
  occupational services since 2018. Additionally, the City has contracted with Keenan &
  Associates since 2018 for ancillary Employee Benefit Programs, which included: Dental
  Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life & Disability Insurance benefits, Voluntary Life Insurance
  benefits, Flexible Spending Account benefits and Employee Assistance Program. As part of
  9

12.  RESOLUTION ACCEPTING PER CAPITA STATE GRANT FUNDS (TRANSFER FROM
THE CITY OF SAN MARINO) UNDER THE PROPOSITION 68 STATEWIDE PARKS
  PROGRAM – F2M25-18, R2M25-5, M2M25-11

  In January 2025, staff was notified from the City of San Marino of unspent Per Capita Grant
  funds under Proposition 68 in the amount of $186,097, which were subject to recapture if not
  immediately committed or can be transferred to another eligible public agency for capital outlay
  or improvements to existing recreation property. City staff was in the process of pursuing
  facility enhancements to the Joslyn Center including roofing and other facility upgrades. The
  project could benefit from any additional funds for the replacement and upgrade of the facility’s
  existing windows and exterior doors. The City of San Marino and Alhambra consulted on this
  topic of transferring San Marino’s remaining Proposition 68 funds. The City’s interest in the
  funds was also conveyed to California State Parks, grant administrators. On January 21, 2025,
  staff received confirmation from the State that the proposed project was an eligible use of
  Proposition 68 funds. The acceptance of the funds required a cover letter from the City
  Manager and an adopted resolution by the City Council memorializing the acceptance of funds.

  Discussion: Councilmember MALONEY commended staff for identifying a potential funding
  source and expressed appreciation. Councilmembers ANDRADE-STADLER, Councilmember
  MAZA, and Mayor WANG echoed their support.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-5: entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra authorizing the City of Alhambra to enter into an
  amendment for Contract Nos. C9801275 and C9802076 with the State of California for the
  Per Capita Grant Program under the California Drought, Water, Parks, Climate, Coastal
  Protection, and Outdoor Access for All Act of 2018 accepting grant funds in the amount of
  $186,097 from the Per Capita Annual Allocation under the Proposition 68 Statewide Parks
  Program; appropriated revenue and expenditure funds; authorized the City Manager, or
  designee, to execute all documents related to grant implementation; and directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-11)
